# Engine noise diagnosis

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Listen for a constant clatter that is loud during cold starts but fades after about 5 seconds of running time. [t772]

[Partial] Inspect the fan clutch and check for damage on the fan mount bearings caused by it. [t317]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Listen for a constant clatter coming from the engine.
2. Note if the sound is loud during cold starts but fades after about 5 seconds of running time.
3. Check if a faint knock persists, especially under hard acceleration.
4. [Partial] Observe if the noise becomes louder and lasts longer when driving in really cold weather without warming up first.

_Procedure reported by [t772]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Note that 2nd Gen water pumps are driven by the timing belt or chain, so they do not need replacement unless there is an issue. [t317]
- Understand that the fan runs on a separate idler bearing bolted to the front of the engine. [t317]
